| $f$ | $Y=1$ | $Y=3$ | $Y=5$ |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| $X=2$ | $\frac{5}{27}$ | $\frac{2}{9}$ | $\frac{1}{9}$ |
| $X=4$ | $\frac{1}{9}$ | $\frac{8}{27}$ | $\frac{2}{27}$ |

Compute ${f}_{Y|X}(3\,|\,4)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.

activity_context.topic_title: Conditional Distributions for Discrete Random Variables

feedback.problem:
| $f$ | $Y=2$ | $Y=4$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $\frac{3}{20}$ | $\frac{7}{20}$ |
| $X=3$ | $\frac{9}{20}$ | $\frac{1}{20}$ |

Compute ${f}_{X|Y}(1\,|\,4)$ given that the discrete random variables $X$ and $Y$ have the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown in the table above.
feedback.worked_solution:
The conditional probability mass function ${f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)$ is defined as

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(x\,|\,y)=P(X=x\,|\,Y=y).
$$

Therefore, we're required to compute the conditional probability

$$
{f}_{X|Y}(1\,|\,4)=P(X=1\,|\,Y=4).
$$

By the multiplication law for conditional probability, we have

$$
P(X=1\,|\,Y=4)=\frac{P(X=1,Y=4)}{P(Y=4)}=\frac{f(1,4)}{{f}_{Y}(4)}
$$

where $f(x,y)$ is the joint probability mass function of $X$ and $Y,$ and ${f}_{Y}(y)$ is the marginal distribution of $Y.$

Recall that the marginal distribution for $Y$ corresponds to the column totals. Thus, 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{Y}(4) & =f(1,4)+f(3,4) \\  & =\frac{7}{20}+\frac{1}{20} \\  & =\frac{2}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

From the given table, $f(1,4)=\frac{7}{20}.$ 

Finally, substituting  ${f}_{Y}(4)=\frac{2}{5}$ and $f(1,4)=\frac{7}{20}$ in our formula above, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{X|Y}(1\,|\,4) & =P(X=1\,|\,Y=4) \\  & =\frac{f(1,4)}{{f}_{Y}(4)} \\  & =\frac{(\frac{7}{20})}{(\frac{2}{5})} \\  & =\frac{7}{8}.\end{aligned}
$$
